name: read-layer-full-over-budget
description: A `read` of a whole layer in `full` form against a model whose components are wide enough that the response would exceed the server's response budget. The request is well-formed and the model is sound; what cannot be done is send the answer, so it is REFUSED with `over-budget` — the eleventh code — carrying `measured` and the narrower requests that would be answered instead. Nothing is truncated: a cut response is one neither side knows the shape of. The chain has one further step below the narrower forms at a layer, a collection or a member slice: the FIRST PAGE of the set, at the size `discover` publishes as `reads.hint_page_size`. It is offered wherever the set is longer than one page, which this layer is not — three components ARE one page, so a page of it is the layer itself and a hint that replays the request is not a step.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with one further component, `WideSWC`, carrying 800 ports on the base's own `IExample` interface. The layer's `full` publication is over the budget; its `summary` and its `index` are far under it.
context.notes: The width is the whole point and it is in the SEED rather than in this file: a vector that inlined half a megabyte of ports would be unreadable and would say nothing the seed's one rule does not. The wide component is otherwise ordinary — a declared interface on every port, a RAM0 budget, an incoming requirement link — so the baseline is valid and the ONLY thing wrong with the exchange is the size of the answer it asks for.

expected.notes: `invalid` because the request AS POSED cannot be answered: the model is not stale, the caller is not unauthorized and nothing is partial — the other three failure classes each say something untrue here. `semantic` because the request conforms to `$defs/readRequest` exactly; only the server, having published the value, can know how big it is. The refusal carries `hints` — `{form: summary}` then `{form: index}`, complete replayable requests in the chain's narrowing order — and `measured`, with the size, the budget and the element count. Exactly those two, and no paged third: the layer is three elements, and the page a hint could offer is the set that has just been refused. A layer longer than one page ends its chain with `{form: <the form that was served>, limit: <reads.hint_page_size>}` instead, which is what turns a wide layer from a dead end into a walk. Both keys are optional in `$defs/errorResult` and no other code sets either, which is what keeps every other negative vector in this directory byte-identical. Sending the request WITHOUT `form` is the accepted case: a layer address answers `summary` by default, so nothing an agent does by default reaches this refusal.
